summary: A UN draft resolution condemning Syria's human rights violations, circulated by European countries and backed by Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, and Morocco, gains support after the Arab League suspended Damascus over its crackdown on democracy protests.

Iraq warns that the fall of Syrian President Bashar al-Assad would bring war to the Middle East, as Syria ignores an Arab League deadline to accept a regional observer mission and the League announces sanctions including an asset freeze and travel bans on 19 regime figures.
Syria agrees to an Arab League monitoring plan allowing observers into the country, after amending the original text, as regional states seek to end the crackdown on protesters.
Arab League observers head to Homs as the city faces an "invasion" by government troops, with France urging Damascus to allow observers access to the violence-hit city.
French television journalist Gilles Jacquier is killed in an apparent mortar attack while covering pro-government demonstrations in Homs, Syria.
The Arab League braces for bloodshed in Syria as protests erupt and armed clashes raise fears of a full-scale civil war, with the head of the Arab League saying he fears a civil war.
Arab League Secretary-General Nabil Elaraby warns that Syria is heading toward civil war as President Bashar al-Assad continues to flout a regional peace plan.

Syrian activists call for nationwide protests under the slogan "We have the right to defend ourselves," signaling a shift toward armed struggle as military councils are set up and the Syrian National Council offers backing to fighters.
Britain and other Western powers launch a diplomatic offensive to secure Russian agreement on a new UN resolution demanding Syrian President Bashar al-Assad stand aside within 15 days.

Russia remains firm in its pledge to veto any U.N. Security Council resolution that could open the door for international military intervention in Syria, as U.N. diplomats report progress on a compromise resolution but challenges remain and about 70 more deaths are reported in Syria.
Russia and China veto a U.N. Security Council resolution on Syria that condemned the government's crackdown on dissent and backed an Arab League plan calling on President Bashar Assad to cede power.

Syria's military sends tanks and other reinforcements toward the restive central city of Homs in what activists describe as preparations for an offensive to retake rebel-held neighborhoods, amid ongoing shelling and clashes.
Defeated Syrian rebels left their stronghold in Baba Amro, Homs, after a bloody 26-day army siege by government forces.
Fighting raged throughout Syria as President Bashar al-Assad sought to put down the revolt that began in March last year, while rebel forces vowed to fight to the last man.
Syrian opposition groups forge military links.

Syrian government troops overran the center of rebel resistance in Homs as opposition fighters retreated after nearly a month of artillery bombardment, while Russia backed a UN Security Council statement demanding humanitarian access.
Syrian security forces executed 47 Syrian soldiers who attempted to defect in the city of Idlib.
U.S. Senator John McCain calls for airstrikes against Syria, becoming the first U.S. leader to call for direct military intervention in the Syrian conflict.
Russia and China begin to edge away from their defense of Syrian President Bashar al-Assad, while U.S. Senator John McCain calls for U.S.-led airstrikes against Syrian forces.
U.N. envoy Kofi Annan meets with Syrian President Bashar al-Assad in Damascus but fails to achieve any breakthrough in mediating an end to Syria's yearlong conflict.

The opposition Syrian National Council called for Western and Arab military intervention and announced it would arm the Free Syrian Army, as internal divisions and defections over the militarization of the uprising intensified.
US President Barack Obama says the prospect of international military intervention in Syria is premature and could lead to a civil war.
Syria marks the first anniversary of the uprising against President Bashar al-Assad, as government forces clear "armed terrorists" from Idlib and supporters of Assad hold rallies across Syria.

The conflict in Syria, which has left thousands dead and stymied international peace efforts, is described by experts including Kofi Annan as a geopolitically significant crisis with potential for regional power shifts, proxy wars, and spreading instability beyond Syria's borders.
Turkey blames Syria for supporting Kurdish rebels and may consider military action, potentially invading Syria if the PKK threat is deemed a national security risk.

Arab leaders at the Baghdad summit urged a peaceful solution to the crisis in Syria and called for talks between the Syrian government and opposition based on Kofi Annan's six-point peace plan, while stopping short of demanding President Bashar al-Assad step down or arming the rebels.
Syrian opposition expresses wariness about a jihadist push.
Syria pledges to observe a ceasefire.
The US calls for a Syrian arms embargo.
Syria holds a parliamentary election that the opposition dismisses as a sham and boycotts, amid continued violence and a failed UN-backed ceasefire.
A bomb explodes near a convoy of UN monitors in Deraa, Syria, wounding eight members of the security forces accompanying them, while violence continues despite the April 12 ceasefire.
The Syrian revolt enters its 15th month of strife, with violence continuing despite a UN-Arab League truce and the United Nations warning Syria is edging closer to full-blown civil war.
Syrian government forces shell Houla.

Following the Houla massacre in which 108 people, including 49 children and 34 women, were killed, UN-Arab League envoy Kofi Annan arrives in Damascus and calls on all armed individuals to lay down their weapons as Syria plunges toward civil war amid escalating clashes and shelling across the country.
Russia and China warn against outside military intervention in Syria and say they will block UN authorization for military action, following the Houla massacre.

Western nations warn that Syria is nearing full-blown sectarian civil war and urge Russia to end its support for President Bashar al-Assad, while rebels press envoy Kofi Annan to declare his peace plan dead.

Russia signals it no longer views Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's position as tenable and is working with the U.S. toward an orderly transition, with a U.S. delegation scheduled to meet Russian counterparts in Moscow on June 8.

The United Nations issues an urgent call to both sides in the Syrian conflict for the evacuation of civilians believed trapped in Homs and Haffah as the Syrian military bombards Homs with helicopter gunships and artillery.

U.S. President Barack Obama and Russian President Vladimir Putin jointly call for an immediate cessation of all violence in Syria, stating they are united in the belief that the Syrian people should independently and democratically choose their own future.

Turkey accuses Syria of shooting down a Turkish military jet in international airspace, saying the unarmed aircraft was on a solo mission to test domestic radar systems and was hit without warning after briefly crossing Syrian airspace.
A conference on Syria aims to reach a transition deal.

World powers at a Geneva meeting back a U.N.-brokered plan for a transitional government in Syria, but the agreement leaves unresolved whether President Bashar Assad would be excluded, with Russia rejecting U.S. insistence that he must go.
Syrian regime forces withdrew from several Kurdish towns and villages near the Turkish border, ceding de facto control to armed Kurdish fighters who set up checkpoints and raised Kurdish flags.
The al-Qaida-inspired Al-Nusra Front claims responsibility for dozens of attacks across Syria, including a June 27 attack on the pro-regime Al-Ikhbariya TV station that killed seven people.
Iraqi Foreign Minister Hoshyar Zebari states that al-Qaeda operatives are infiltrating Syria across Iraq's western border, warning that the Syrian conflict risks spilling over into Iraq.
Iraqi-Kurdish leader Massoud Barzani brokers a deal between rival Syrian-Kurdish groups, forming a national council to pursue common Kurdish interests.
Syria confirms it has chemical weapons.
Syrian regime renews its assault on Aleppo.
Syrian troops shot and killed a 6-year-old boy as he fled with his family into Jordan, the first such fatality among refugees crossing the border.
Syrian regime forces concentrate elite troops and heavy weaponry for an all-out assault to recapture rebel-seized parts of Aleppo, as the opposition braces for a major battle.
Syrian government forces launch a ground assault and heavy artillery bombardment on rebel-held areas of Aleppo, as rebels say they repelled the first wave of attacks and fighting continues.
Christians in Aleppo and elsewhere in Syria are taking up arms, often supplied by the Assad regime, amid fears of sectarian bloodletting as foreign and local radicals rise in Syria's civil war.

Syrian government troops bombard Aleppo's Salaheddine district with tank and artillery fire as rebels consolidate their hold on seized areas, with analysts saying the battle for Aleppo is likely to be more protracted than the earlier clashes in Damascus.
Fighting continues in Syria.

Security experts say al Qaeda is being reinvigorated by the Syrian crisis, as Sunni militants travel to Syria to fight President Bashar al-Assad, gaining funds, recruits and morale that also fuel a revival of al Qaeda's Iraqi affiliate.
Former UN secretary-general Kofi Annan resigns as special envoy of the UN and League of Arab States for Syria.

The battle for Aleppo, Syria's second-largest city and economic capital, is described as the decisive battle for the entire country, with rebels claiming to have taken six neighborhoods and an important border crossing into Turkey while the Syrian regime denies those claims.
Syrian government forces launch a ground offensive on rebel-held areas of Aleppo, while fighter jets carry out airstrikes on the nearby village of Tel Rifat, killing six members of the same family.
Syrian Kurds are moving to establish an autonomous region in northern Syria, adding complexity to the conflict.
Syrian government forces pushed rebels back from the strategic Salaheddine district of Aleppo, though skirmishes continued in the city.
A Syrian rebel commander in Aleppo warns the West that if it does not provide more help, his forces will forge an alliance with Al Qaeda.

Syria's archaeological and architectural heritage, including UNESCO World Heritage Sites such as Aleppo, Apamea, and Krac des Chevaliers, has been damaged or is under threat from shelling and looting amid the ongoing Syrian conflict.

President Obama says the use or deployment of chemical or biological weapons by the Assad regime would be a "red line" that could prompt the U.S. to reconsider military involvement in Syria, though he did not say such use would necessarily trigger an American military response.

Al Qaeda-sympathetic fighters, including the group Jabhat al-Nusra, are gaining strength and numbers within the Syrian conflict, operating independently and pushing the uprising toward a struggle for an Islamic state.

Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Gennady Gatilov says Syria has given Russia clear assurances it will not use or move its chemical weapons stockpiles, following a US warning that Washington might intervene if Damascus did so.

Iraqi troops exchange fire with unidentified gunmen and come under rocket attack near the al-Qaim border crossing with Syria, as Iraq tightens border controls to curb spillover from the Syrian crisis and Syrian army shelling hits an Iraqi border town.
Syrian President Bashar al-Assad says the situation in Syria is "now better" but that he needs more time to "win the battle."
The U.N. reports that 100,000 Syrian refugees fled the country in August, the largest monthly total since the conflict began 17 months earlier.
Egyptian President Mohamed Morsy calls for a transitional phase in Syria and for Bashar al-Assad to leave power during a meeting of Arab League foreign ministers in Cairo.

A car bombing near two hospitals in western Aleppo kills 27 civilians and wounds 64, according to Syrian state media, while opposition activists report at least 160 people killed across Syria the previous day.
A Syrian air strike reportedly hits a fuel station in the northern province of al-Raqqa, killing at least 54 people, according to a British-based violence watchdog.
An air strike in Syria reportedly killed 20 people.
Fighting continues in Syria.
Fighting between government and rebel forces in Aleppo causes a fire that badly damages the medieval souk, a UNESCO World Heritage site, destroying much of the ancient market.
A wave of suicide car bombings and explosions targeting Syrian government forces kills dozens of people at a popular square in Aleppo, an attack claimed by the al-Nusra Front.
Turkey's parliament authorizes cross-border military operations in Syria after a Syrian mortar strike killed five Turkish civilians, prompting Turkish retaliation and international condemnation.

Turkish officials declare Turkey has no intention of war with Syria even as lawmakers authorize further military operations and Turkish artillery strikes Syrian positions for a second day, following a Syrian shelling that killed five in a Turkish border town.

Turkish artillery fires into Syria for the fourth consecutive day in retaliation for mortar shells from Syria that landed in Turkish territory, as Syrian rebels clash with government troops in the border area of Idlib province.
Turkish artillery fires across the border into Syria, with explosions damaging buildings in Aleppo, as part of escalating violence in the Syrian conflict.

Syrian shelling across the border into Turkey continues for a sixth consecutive day, prompting Turkish retaliation and a parliamentary authorization for cross-border military operations, while Turkey floats a political transition proposal involving Syrian Vice President Farouk al-Sharaa.

Syrian Islamist rebel brigades announce the formation of a new united front against President Bashar al-Assad, claiming more than 40,000 fighters, though the front excludes some groups Western officials consider most radical and its formation widens rifts with other rebels.

A group of Syrian army soldiers fleeing a rebel assault crossed into Turkey, with Free Syrian Army fighters capturing 10 and turning them over to Turkish authorities, while a Syrian helicopter's approach prompted Turkey to scramble two F-16 fighter jets.

Syrian rebels, including the Al Qaeda-linked Al Nusra Front, seized a government missile defense base near Aleppo after hours of fighting, though government fighter jets subsequently attacked the base and destroyed the missiles.
A landmark mosque in Aleppo, the Umayyad Mosque, was burned and damaged amid fighting between Syrian rebels and government troops, with both sides blaming each other for the destruction.
Syrian government forces retake control of the Umayyad Mosque in Aleppo after rebels had captured it during clashes.

Turkey accuses Syria of supplying weapons and support to the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) as tensions between the former allies escalate, with Damascus allegedly using the PKK as a proxy to retaliate against Ankara's backing of the Free Syrian Army and its push for regime change in Syria.

International peace envoy Lakhdar Brahimi travels to Iran to seek help in brokering a ceasefire in Syria, proposing a truce during the Eid holiday starting around October 25, as fighting continues in Aleppo and other cities.
The Syrian government says it is ready to explore a four-day truce proposed by international envoy Lakhdar Brahimi, even as it steps up aerial assaults on rebel positions in the north.
A car bomb in central Beirut kills a top Lebanese intelligence official and seven others, an attack widely linked to heightened tensions over the war in neighboring Syria.

UN envoy Lakhdar Brahimi calls for a brief ceasefire in Syria during the Eid al-Adha holiday, a call joined by Turkey, Germany, and Iran, though activists report continued regime airstrikes in Idlib province.

A Jordanian soldier is killed in clashes with armed militants trying to cross the border into Syria, marking the first member of Jordan's military killed in violence related to Syria's civil war, as the conflict spills across borders into Jordan and Lebanon.
The Syrian regime agrees in principle to a cease-fire proposed by U.N. envoy Lakhdar Brahimi to cover the Eid al-Adha holiday, though rebels remain skeptical and no formal statement has been issued.
An al-Qaida-inspired militant group in Syria rejects a cease-fire proposed by international envoy Lakhdar Brahimi for the Eid al-Adha holiday.
The Syrian government and the Free Syrian Army say they will halt military operations during the Muslim holiday of Eid al-Adha, though the truce's terms and durability remain uncertain.
Clashes erupt in Aleppo between the Free Syrian Army and the Kurdish People's Defense Units militia, killing about 30 people.

A four-day ceasefire in Syria ended bloodily as a car bomb killed ten people in Damascus and government jets bombed the suburbs, with the truce accepted by President Bashar al-Assad's regime and several rebel groups failing to stop the violence.

The United States and other governments, through public warnings by President Obama and private messages relayed via Russia, Iraq, Turkey and possibly Jordan, deterred Syrian President Bashar al-Assad from using chemical weapons, halting chemical mixing and bomb preparation during a week from late November to early December, though concerns remained that Assad could deploy the weapons at any moment.

As many as 11,000 people fled Syria in a 24-hour period, with about 9,000 crossing into Turkey and 1,000 each into Jordan and Lebanon, amid fierce fighting between rebels and government forces for control of the border town of Ras al-Ayn.
Rebels have to find common voice in battle against Assad.

Israel shelled Syrian fighters after gunfire from the Syrian civil war spilled over into the Israel-controlled Golan Heights, with the military reporting a hit but not knowing whether the targets were rebels or forces loyal to President Bashar Assad.
A group of 13 extremist Islamist factions in Syria rejects the newly formed Western-backed opposition coalition and declares Aleppo an "Islamic state."
Syria loses influence among Palestinians.
Syrian rebels capture an army artillery base on the outskirts of Mayadeen in Deir Az-Zor province, further weakening government control in the strategic region bordering Iraq.

Syrian government jets bomb a rebel base near the Turkish border, one of the closest strikes to the border carried out by Syrian jets, as rebels tighten their hold around Damascus and Turkey prepares to deploy Patriot missiles.
Two Iraqi men, one Sunni and one Shiite, describe fighting on opposing sides in Syria, framing the conflict as an extension of the sectarian war in Iraq.
Concerns persist over the threat posed by Assad's chemical weapons stocks in the Syrian conflict, with challenges for both the US and Russia.

NATO warns Syrian President Bashar Assad that any use of chemical weapons would be met with an immediate international response, as NATO foreign ministers are expected to agree to send Patriot missiles to Turkey.

A senior U.S. official reports that Syrian forces have mixed chemical weapons, including sarin, and loaded them into bombs for potential use against President Bashar Assad's own people, though the bombs have not yet been loaded onto planes and require Assad's order for use.
NATO moves forward with plans to deploy Patriot missiles and troops along Syria's border with Turkey to protect against potential attacks, a move Syria's regime condemns as "psychological warfare."

US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, and UN peace envoy Lakhdar Brahimi meet in Belfast and proclaim progress toward an agreement on a political transition to stop Syria's civil war.
The US issues a warning regarding Syrian chemical weapons.

U.S. intelligence indicates Syria has recently loaded mixed nerve agents into aerial bombs near Syrian airfields, raising Western concerns about possible military action, while U.S. and Russian officials meet in Dublin with mediator Lakhdar Brahimi to seek a strategy to end Syria's civil war.
The U.S. State Department designates the anti-Assad rebel group Jabhat al-Nusra as an "international terrorist organization."
Syrian rebels seize most of a military academy outside Aleppo after weeks of fighting with regime troops, according to opposition activists.
Russia states it will serve its national interests in pressing Syrian President Bashar Assad to go.
Syrian rebels and Palestinian fighters loyal to President Bashar al-Assad battled for control of the Yarmouk Palestinian refugee camp in south Damascus, forcing refugees to flee the area.

Syrian government forces carry out a broad offensive against rebels in the suburbs of Damascus, while opposition fighters take control of large parts of the Yarmouk Palestinian refugee camp after clashes with a pro-regime faction.

The UN launches a $1.5bn appeal to fund aid over the next six months for Syrians inside Syria and refugees in neighbouring countries, warning that refugee numbers could double to more than a million by June.
Balance of military power shifts in Syria, with pressures on Assad offering a chance to test diplomatic prospects.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Syria's civil war has reached a stalemate and that international efforts to persuade President Bashar al-Assad to quit will fail, stating Assad "is not going anywhere."
Syria's military police chief, Major General Abdelaziz Jassim al-Shalal, defected from the army and declared allegiance to the uprising against President Bashar al-Assad.
International envoy Lakhdar Brahimi proposes a transitional government for Syria, a plan backed by Russia but rejected by the main opposition council.

The armed conflict between President Bashar al-Assad's regime and opposition fighters continues as UN-Arab League envoy Lakhdar Brahimi says a diplomatic solution remains possible despite a sharply deteriorating situation.

U.N. Human Rights Commissioner Navi Pillay says at least 60,000 people have died in Syria's conflict, citing a U.N.-commissioned study that documented 59,648 reported deaths between March 15, 2011, and November 30, 2012.

Syrian President Bashar al-Assad offers a plan to end fighting, including a conditional cease-fire, a new constitution, and expanded government, in a televised address that was quickly rejected by opposition groups and Western governments.
Syrian President Bashar Assad delivers a defiant speech at the Damascus Opera House, rejecting negotiations with the opposition and vowing to continue fighting the 21-month-old rebellion.
The World Food Program says Syria's civil war has blocked the U.N. agency from delivering aid to at least 1 million people in desperate need of help.

The Nusra Front, Syria's largest jihadist rebel group, says it stands with other Syrian rebels and fights alongside the Free Syrian Army, despite its extremist ideology and the U.S. designation of it as a foreign terrorist organization.

UN envoy Lakhdar Brahimi says Syrian President Bashar al-Assad will have no place in any transitional government following the civil war, while also stating there is no military solution and negotiations should occur in 2013.
Syrian rebels and Islamic militants captured the strategic Taftanaz air base in Idlib province, seizing helicopters, tanks and multiple rocket launchers in a significant blow to government forces.
International envoy Lakhdar Brahimi's talks in Geneva with Russian and U.S. officials end without a deal, and he says he does not expect a political solution to Syria's civil war anytime soon.
Syria's Foreign Ministry denounces international envoy Lakhdar Brahimi as "flagrantly biased" ahead of Geneva talks, while remaining willing to work with him on a political solution.

Syrian fighter jets carry out lethal airstrikes on rebel strongholds near Damascus, with eight children reported killed in Moadamiyeh, as at least 57 countries call on the UN Security Council to refer the Syria conflict to the International Criminal Court for a war crimes investigation.

An international aid agency reports that Syria's civil war is causing a staggering humanitarian crisis in the Middle East, with over 600,000 Syrians having fled abroad, many citing gang rape and sexual violence as reasons for fleeing.
A rocket strike on a residential building in regime-held Aleppo and two suicide car bombs near a mosque in Daraa cap a bloody week in Syria's civil war, with more than 800 civilians killed.

The U.N. refugee agency warns that the Syrian refugee crisis is the fastest-deteriorating humanitarian crisis on the planet, with more than 670,000 refugees registered in neighboring countries and the forecast of 1 million by June on track to be surpassed well before that.

Syrian government forces escalate a rocket and artillery offensive against rebel-held areas in the central Homs province, as at least 140 people are reported killed in nationwide fighting and a record number of Syrians flee into Jordan.

Israeli jets struck a target inside Syria, reported as a convoy carrying SA-17 anti-aircraft missiles for Hezbollah, while Syrian state media said the strike hit a defense research center in Jamraya, killing at least two people.

Jordan faces mounting economic and security strains from the Syrian conflict, hosting more than 330,000 Syrian refugees and warning that prolonged fighting or fragmentation of Syria would be catastrophic for the region.

Israel's defense minister indicates Israel was behind a January 30 airstrike in Syria that U.S. officials said targeted anti-aircraft weapons believed bound for Hezbollah, while Syrian President Bashar Assad says Syria can confront any aggression.

Leaders of Islamic states at an Organisation of Islamic Cooperation summit in Cairo call for a peaceful resolution to the Syrian conflict through "serious dialogue" between the regime and its foes, while Iran, Iraq, and Lebanon voice reservations about the statement on Syria.
Syrian rebels captured a military air base near Aleppo and stormed another protecting the city's international airport, a day after seizing the country's largest dam.

Syrian rebels fought government forces at a military base protecting Aleppo International Airport, with opposition activists saying more than 40 government troops were killed, though the airport itself remained in regime hands.

UN human rights investigators identify Syrian leaders on both sides of the civil war who may be responsible for war crimes and call on the Security Council to refer the violations to the International Criminal Court.

A UN-appointed panel of inquiry warns that Syria's civil war is becoming increasingly sectarian and that both sides are becoming more radicalized, partly due to the growing presence of foreign fighters, and urges the international community to curb the supply of weapons.

More than 81,000 Syrian Kurds have fled Syria's civil war to northern Iraq's autonomous Kurdish region in recent months, with few in a rush to return home amid mixed feelings about a future without Bashar Assad.
A car bomb targeting the headquarters of Syria's ruling Baath Socialist Party in central Damascus kills 53 people and wounds more than 230, with no group immediately claiming responsibility.
The battle for Syria's Aleppo airport intensifies as government troops try to reverse recent rebel gains in the northeast.

Syrian rebels used captured tanks to launch a fresh offensive on a government complex housing a police academy in the northern city of Aleppo, as they continued to log strategic victories against President Bashar Assad's troops.

In the Kurdish autonomous zone in north-east Syria, the PKK-aligned Democratic Union Party (PYD) dominates governance in towns such as Derik, while YPG fighters clash with Islamist rebels of Jabhat al-Nusra and Ghuraba al-Sham in Sere Kaniyeh, as Kurds seek self-government within a democratic Syria amid the ongoing civil war.
Syria and Iran say Assad will remain in power until 2014 presidential elections, as Syrian forces regain control of villages along a key highway to Aleppo.

Syrian President Bashar Assad accuses the U.S. and Britain of supporting terrorism by sending aid to opposition fighters, as activists report more than 200 soldiers and rebels killed in an eight-day battle for a police academy near Aleppo.

The Syrian civil war spills into Iraq when a convoy carrying 65 Assad troops and officials, who had fled across the border after rebels led by Jabhat al-Nusra attacked the Yaarabiya border crossing, is ambushed in Iraq's Anbar province, leaving 42 Syrians and seven Iraqi police dead.
The city of ar-Raqqah in eastern Syria falls to rebel forces, becoming the first provincial capital captured by insurgents, with the offensive led entirely by jihadi forces including Jabhat al-Nusra.

A convoy carrying wounded Syrian soldiers was ambushed in Iraq's western Anbar province, killing 48 Syrian soldiers and nine Iraqi guards, an attack Iraq's defence ministry attributed to a Syrian "terrorist group."
Syrian jets bomb opposition-held buildings in the northern city of Raqqa, a day after rebels overran the onetime regime stronghold and captured its provincial governor.
The number of Syrian refugees reaches one million, with more than 7,000 people arriving in Jordan, Lebanon, Turkey and Iraq every day.

A recently distributed video highlights that Islamic militants from Russia's Chechnya region, led by Omar Abu al-Chechen, are fighting alongside Syrian rebels in the jihad against President Bashar al-Assad, with dozens and possibly 100 North Caucasus fighters reported in Syria.
The number of refugees fleeing Syria's civil war reaches one million, with aid agencies including Oxfam struggling to cope with the flood of new arrivals.
New clashes erupt as Syrian rebels intensify their battle to capture Aleppo's international airport and nearby military air bases from government forces.
The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees warns that the Syria crisis is escalating at an unprecedented pace and represents an existential threat to Lebanon.

Lebanese citizens in Tripoli and across Lebanon are growing weary of the steady influx of Syrian refugees, blaming them for shrinking wages, job losses, and rising rents and prices, amid fears the refugee crisis could destabilize Lebanon's fragile political and social balance.

Both sides in the Syrian civil war traded accusations over the use of chemical weapons, with the regime and rebels blaming each other for attacks in Aleppo's Khan al-Assal area and the Damascus suburb of east Ghouta, though the claims were not proven.

U.S. officials warn that Syria's refugee crisis could quadruple to 4 million by the end of 2013 if the civil war continues, with UN High Commissioner for Refugees António Guterres telling Congress that 8,000 people a day were fleeing Syria in February.

Syria's government and rebels both demand an international investigation into an alleged chemical weapons attack in the northern village of Khan al-Assal that killed at least 31 people, each side blaming the other.
Israeli intelligence sources say chemical weapons were likely used in a Syrian attack on 2013-03-18, though the claim remains unconfirmed and Syria, Russia, and rebels trade accusations.
The UN announces it will investigate an alleged chemical weapons attack near Aleppo, Syria, after Britain pressed for a full inquiry, though Russia blocked attempts to widen the probe's scope.

UN High Commissioner for Refugees Antonio Guterres warns that the Syrian refugee crisis spilling over into Lebanon would be an "existential threat," as the number of registered Syrian refugees jumps 10 percent in one week to more than 1.1 million.
Dozens of nations at the UN Human Rights Council agree to extend a UN probe of human rights abuses in Syria's civil war for another year.

The United Nations launches an investigation into claims by the Syrian government and rebels that either side used chemical weapons in the conflict, as preliminary U.S. analysis indicates chemical weapons were not used by the regime.

Syrian rebels advance on the ground, seizing territory in the south and firing one of the heaviest mortar volleys yet into central Damascus, while the opposition leadership falls deeper into disarray as Syrian National Coalition head Mouaz al-Khatib announces he is stepping down and 10 other members suspend their membership.

Lebanon calls for its Syrian refugees to be transferred to other Arab countries to share the burden, as it projects those fleeing the violence will account for half its population by the end of the year.

The United Nations hopes that a team investigating allegations about the use of chemical weapons in Syria's civil war will deploy to the country as early as next week, though that may not be possible since the experts need to be assembled and approved and the investigation's mandate clarified.

Syrian rebels pushed into the strategic Sheikh Maqsoud neighborhood in Aleppo after days of heavy clashes, with conflicting reports about the scale of their advance and the killing of a pro-government cleric captured in the fighting.

Syria's ancient oasis city of Palmyra is being damaged in clashes between President Bashar al-Assad's forces and rebels fighting for his overthrow, with shelling and gunfire striking the archaeological site.

The head of a United Nations refugee agency warns that refugees from Syria's war are on the verge of overwhelming the United Nations and neighboring host countries, predicting the flow will swamp their resources by the end of the year.

Syria's state news media lashes out at Jordan and Turkey, accusing them of supporting rebels, as part of an intensified propaganda response to rebel gains and President Bashar al-Assad's further isolation.
Human Rights Watch reports that more than 4,300 civilians have been killed in Syrian government airstrikes since July 2012, documenting 59 unlawful attacks in northern Syria.

New figures highlight the scale of the human tragedy in Syria's escalating civil war, with some 4 million people trapped inside the country, 1.2 million refugees having fled across borders, and reconstruction costs estimated at $80 billion even if the violence were to stop.
The Al Qaeda-affiliated Islamic State of Iraq announces it has united with Syria's Al Nusra Front, forming the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria.
Jordan opens a second camp, Mrajeeb Fhood, to shelter increasing numbers of refugees fleeing Syria's civil war.
Syria's al-Nusra Front rebel group pledges allegiance to al Qaeda leader Ayman al-Zawahri and joins with al Qaeda's Iraq branch to form the Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant.

A senior Israeli military intelligence official accuses Syrian President Bashar Assad of using lethal chemical weapons, probably sarin, against insurgents in a series of incidents over recent months, including an attack near Damascus on March 19.

The United Nations says the Syria conflict has become a humanitarian catastrophe, prompting the deadlocked Security Council to agree on a non-binding statement demanding an end to the escalating violence and condemning human rights abuses by all sides.
Syrian rebels captured large parts of the Dabaa military complex in Homs province near the Lebanese border, though sporadic fighting was still ongoing in some parts of the base.

UN High Commissioner for Refugees António Guterres warns that more than half of Syria's population will likely need aid by the end of the year, calling the Syrian civil war the most serious humanitarian crisis the UN has dealt with.
Members of the Syrian opposition express caution ahead of an upcoming Friends of Syria meeting in Istanbul, saying they expect concrete results rather than promises of support.
Kurdish women fighters, including a female commander, are battling in Syria's armed rebellion in Aleppo, with the YPG brigade being 20 percent women.

An Israeli intelligence official alleges that Syrian forces have likely used chemical weapons, including sarin gas, against rebels on multiple occasions, while the U.S. says it has not confirmed the claim and Russia warns against jumping to conclusions.

US Secretary of State John Kerry warns NATO that preparations must be made for the threat posed by chemical weapons in Syria, amid claims that President Bashar al-Assad's forces have already carried out attacks using Sarin nerve gas.

U.S. pressure mounts to intervene in Syria after the Assad regime allegedly used chemical weapons, with lawmakers urging action and the White House pressing the UN to investigate while saying no option is off the table if use is proven.
The White House says the U.S. intelligence community assesses with varying degrees of confidence that the Syrian regime has used chemical weapons, specifically sarin, on a small scale in Syria.
A former Hezbollah leader alleges that Iran pressed Hezbollah fighters to join the civil war in Syria to support President Bashar al-Assad, saying at least 138 militiamen had died there.

President Barack Obama says that use of chemical weapons by Syria's Bashar al-Assad would change his "calculus" over launching military action, while stating that too little is known about alleged sarin attacks to justify it now.
Syrian Information Minister Omran Al-Zoubi denies that Syria possesses or has used chemical weapons, accusing the United States and Britain of lying to pressure the Damascus government.
Kurdish militia group the Popular Protection Unit clashes with Free Syrian Army rebels in Aleppo, Syria, killing several people including an 8-year-old boy.
Syrian Information Minister Omran al-Zoubi denies U.S. charges that Syrian troops used chemical weapons, saying the accusation resulted from recent army victories over rebels.

Jordan faces an escalating Syrian refugee crisis, with funding shortfalls threatening aid operations in the Za'ateri camp and the number of Syrian refugees in Jordan expected to rise to 1.2 million by the end of the year.

Oxfam calls for improved humanitarian access to Syria, warning that the humanitarian crisis is at its worst point since the conflict erupted two years ago and urging the UN Security Council to help ensure aid reaches those most in need.

UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon says investigators are gathering and analyzing information on alleged chemical weapons attacks in Syria but that Syrian authorities have blocked unconditional access needed for a credible on-site inquiry, and he again urges Syria to allow the investigation to proceed without delay and without conditions.

A powerful bomb explodes in the Marjeh commercial district of central Damascus, killing 13 people and wounding 70, according to Syrian state TV, in an attack described by the government as a "terrorist bombing."

President Barack Obama says the United States must be more certain of all the facts regarding the use of chemical weapons by Syrian leader Bashar Assad before deciding how to intervene in the conflict.
Iran declares the alleged use of chemical weapons by anyone in Syria a "red line," reiterating calls for a UN investigation into Syrian government assertions that insurgents used chemical weapons.

President Obama says he would consider U.S. military action against Syria if hard, effective evidence confirms chemical weapons use, while officials draft options including lethal aid to rebels, a no-fly zone, and targeted missile strikes, none of which have been decided.

Syria's U.N. ambassador Bashar Ja'afari says the use of chemical weapons is a "blood line" that cannot be tolerated and demands a U.N. investigation of an alleged chemical weapons attack in Aleppo that Syria blames on rebels.
President Obama says he will not rush to act against Syria over chemical weapons, stressing that U.S. intelligence does not yet know how, when, or by whom they were used.

Syrian government troops took control of large swaths of territory in Homs, including the Wadi al-Sayah neighborhood, encircling an opposition suburb and gaining direct access to the Old District stronghold.

Israeli warplanes struck areas in and around Damascus, targeting a shipment of Iranian-made guided missiles believed bound for Hezbollah, in the second such attack in three days; Syria's state media reported the strikes hit a military and scientific research center and caused casualties, and the Syrian government condemned the attacks.

A UN inquiry investigator says there are strong but not incontrovertible suspicions that rebel forces used sarin gas in Syria, while the UN commission says it has not reached conclusive findings and the White House says it is highly skeptical of the suggestion.

Eight Syrian government security troops were killed when their helicopter was shot down in eastern Syria, according to Syrian opposition forces, as reports emerged that rebels may have used chemical weapons.
Syria says an Israeli attack on a military site was a "declaration of war."

The International Committee of the Red Cross urges both sides in Syria's civil war to allow swift evacuation of the dead and wounded, many of them civilians, who often lie abandoned for days or months in intense urban fighting.
Turkey launches a military exercise near the Syrian border.

U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry departs for Moscow to attempt to revive a U.S.-Russian political solution to end Syria's civil war, though it is uncertain whether the two countries can move forward on the Geneva plan they endorsed on 2012-06-30.
U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow to seek common ground on ending Syria's civil war, though Putin made no public mention of the conflict.

U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov announce a joint diplomatic effort to convene an international conference aimed at bringing the Syrian government and opposition together to form a transitional government, while leaving President Bashar al-Assad's fate vague.
Israeli airstrikes in Syria target Iranian weapons destined for Hezbollah, with Syrian officials branding the strikes a declaration of war while Assad vows his forces are capable of facing Israel.

The Obama administration's reliance on the Arab League for intervention in Syria is criticized as breeding paralysis, as the Arab League condemns Israel instead of requesting UN intervention while the Assad regime's crackdown continues.
Britain says it is "very likely" the Syrian government has used chemical weapons, while Turkey steps up testing of people fleeing the Syrian civil war for traces.

U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry says that Russia supplying advanced missile systems to Syria would be destabilizing for Israel's security, amid reports of an imminent Russian sale of S-300 air defense missiles to the Assad regime.
US Secretary of State John Kerry and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov agree that America and Russia will jointly convene an international conference on Syria.
British Prime Minister David Cameron and Russian President Vladimir Putin meet in Sochi to discuss joint options for ending the crisis in Syria, with no immediate breakthrough.
Turkey says Syrian casualties treated in Turkey show signs of being victims of chemical weapons, adding to indications that the use of such arms may have occurred.

U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry warns that Russia's planned transfer of advanced missile defense systems to Syria would be a destabilizing factor for Israel's security, as Damascus welcomes a U.S.-Russian initiative for peace talks while vowing immediate retaliation to any new Israeli airstrike.

Russia says there is disagreement over who should represent the opposition in a Syrian peace process, days after Moscow and Washington announced a joint effort to bring government and rebels to an international conference.
The European Commission announces an additional 65 million euros in aid for Syrian refugees and internally displaced people, warning the crisis is already at breaking point.

Syrian Information Minister Omran al-Zoubi says the government wants more details before deciding whether to take part in a proposed U.S.-Russian initiative to negotiate a peaceful end to Syria's crisis.
The number of Syrian refugees registered or awaiting registration tops 1.5 million, according to UNHCR figures.
Syrian rebels withdrew from Aleppo prison after heavy fighting with government troops failed to free prisoners, as the death toll from May 3 sectarian killings in Banias was raised to 145.
US President Obama reveals the US has evidence that chemical weapons were used in Syria, a use he had previously said would cross a "red line," while Russia sends advanced missiles to aid Assad.

A six-member U.N. team led by former Syrian planning minister Abdullah al-Dardari is drawing up a comprehensive postwar reconstruction plan for Syria, estimating at least $60 billion in damage, even as the civil war continues with no apparent end in sight.

UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon says a proposed international conference to try to stop Syria's civil war should be held as soon as possible, though no date has been agreed and the meeting faces growing obstacles.
Hezbollah militants attack the Syrian rebel-held town of Qusair alongside Syrian troops, while Israel threatens more strikes on Syria to rein in the militia.
Kurdish female fighters have joined Syria's armed rebellion as Assad's forces push forward into rebel-held land near the Lebanese border.
Syrian government forces press an offensive in the strategic rebel-held city of Qusair near the Lebanese border, with conflicting accounts of the fighting and at least 90 deaths reported in two days.

Hezbollah fighters are drawn deeper into Syria's civil war as 28 of its members are killed and dozens wounded while fighting rebels in Qusair, part of a government offensive to secure a corridor from Damascus to the Mediterranean coast.

Three more Hezbollah fighters died of wounds sustained in the battle for the Syrian town of Qusair, raising Hezbollah's losses to 31 since Sunday as Syrian government forces backed by Hezbollah pushed deeper into the opposition-held town.
Sectarian tensions in Iraq, worsened by spillover from the Syrian civil war, test Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki's government as Sunni protests and attacks continue.
Syrian rebels fighting for control of Qusair call for reinforcements to repel forces loyal to President Bashar al-Assad, as violence spills over Syria's borders.
A senior U.N. official says the United Nations is receiving mounting reports of chemical weapons use in Syria's civil war, as U.N.-Syria negotiations on access for investigators remain deadlocked.

Syrian deputy foreign minister Faisal Mekdad holds extensive negotiations in Moscow over whether the Assad regime will participate in the Geneva conference, without announcing whether Syria would take part.

The head of the U.N. Relief and Works Agency said that 70 to 80 percent of the 530,000 Palestinians in Syria have been affected by the civil war, with more than half displaced from their homes, and appealed to the Syrian government and rebel fighters to allow aid deliveries to the Palestinian camps.
Russia says the Syrian regime has agreed in principle to attend June Geneva peace talks, though the Syrian opposition calls for Damascus to confirm directly.

Hezbollah leader Hasan Nasrallah publicly defends sending his fighters to support President Bashar al-Assad’s army in Syria and promises victory, as Hezbollah and government forces escalate an assault on the Syrian town of Qusair.
Syrian refugees resume crossing into Jordan after a weeklong lull, with 141 refugees entering early Saturday, though Jordanian officials denied reports that border guards had turned back refugees.

Syrian government forces and Hezbollah launch a fierce artillery and ground campaign to seize rebel-held territory in the border town of Qusair, killing more than 22 people in opposition-held areas by that afternoon.

Rockets hit a Hezbollah stronghold outside Beirut, injuring at least four people, hours after Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah vowed victory in Syria's war and said thousands of his fighters were ready to fight alongside Syrian government forces.
Syrian Foreign Minister Walid al-Moallem says his government agrees "in principle" to attend an international Geneva peace conference proposed by Russia and the United States.
Syria and the opposition agree in principle to attend a peace conference.

More than 54,000 Palestinian refugees have fled the civil war in Syria for Lebanon since the beginning of the 2011 uprising, compounding decades of statelessness and straining aid agencies in Lebanon.

Hopes for a proposed international peace conference on Syria may be dashed as fighting shows signs of turning into a sectarian-fueled conflagration that pulls in neighbors and pits world powers against one another.
Israel threatens to strike Russian S-300 air defence missiles en route to Syria, while Russia says it has no reason to revise its stance on the deal despite Western and Israeli criticism.

Syrian Foreign Minister Walid al-Moallem says Bashar Assad will remain president at least until elections in 2014 and might seek another term, adding that any deal reached in proposed U.N.-sponsored talks would have to be put to a referendum.
Iran expresses support for international talks in Geneva to end Syria's civil war.
Russia agrees to send S-300 missile defense batteries to the Syrian army amid ongoing arms supplies to the government of President Bashar al-Assad.

International officials and diplomats preparing make-or-break Syria peace talks in Geneva have not yet been able to persuade senior representatives from either side of the civil war to participate, leaving the negotiations in doubt.
The Syrian government confirms for the first time that it will attend the planned Geneva peace talks on Syria, though it has not decided on the makeup of its delegation.
Syria's foreign minister and the main Western-backed opposition group issue terms that would make it difficult for U.S.-Russian sponsored peace talks on ending Syria's civil war to succeed.
Syria has reportedly received its first shipment of Russian S-300 air defence missiles, according to comments attributed to President Bashar al-Assad.

Syria's main Western-backed opposition group, the Syrian National Coalition, says it will not participate in U.S.-Russian sponsored peace talks while massacres are underway and will not support international peace efforts in light of Iran's and Hezbollah's "invasion" of Syria.
Jordan closes its northern border with Syria, turning away thousands of Syrians fleeing the civil war, including women and children, leaving them stranded and vulnerable.

The United States warns Russia against transferring advanced S-300 long-range missiles to Syria, saying the sale threatens Israel and regional stability, while Syrian President Bashar al-Assad says he will fulfill all existing weapons contracts with Russia and threatens immediate retaliation to any attack.

Syrian rebels plead for military and medical aid in the besieged border town of Qusair, saying they are unable to evacuate hundreds of wounded under an onslaught from government forces backed by Lebanese Hezbollah fighters.
Britain informs U.N. Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon of additional suspected chemical weapons attacks by Syrian government forces in March and April.

Reports indicate Russia's S-300 air defense missiles may not reach Syria until 2014, with Russian sources saying no missiles have been delivered so far and delivery could begin no earlier than autumn 2013.
Syria peace talks in Geneva are almost certain to be postponed after Russia announces plans to ship more weapons, including MiG fighter jets, to the Assad regime.

Syrian troops and Hezbollah guerrillas besieging the border town of Qusair fought with rebels as the United Nations warned all sides they would be held accountable for the suffering of trapped civilians.
Syrian rebels brace for a fresh assault on Qusair by the army and its Hezbollah allies, after fierce fighting the previous day in the north of the town, with concerns about civilians trapped there.

The Syrian town of Qusair near the Lebanese border has become the latest site of urban warfare in the grueling fight between President Bashar Assad's military and the rebels trying to overthrow his regime, with the battle raging on for a third straight week.
The British and French governments announce that medical samples smuggled out of Syria have tested positive for the nerve agent sarin, and say they have shown the evidence to a UN investigation.

United Nations human rights investigators say they have "reasonable grounds" to believe that limited amounts of chemical weapons had been used in Syria, with most testimony relating to their use by government forces.
Syrian troops and their Lebanese Hezbollah allies captured the strategic border town of Qusair after a three-week battle, dealing a severe blow to rebels.
Syrian rebels capture a crossing point along the cease-fire line in the contested Golan Heights patrolled by U.N. troops, though Syrian state TV denies the rebels control the Quneitra crossing.
Syrian Prime Minister Wael al-Halaqi says the government's capture of al-Qusair is a "strategic turning point" marking the beginning of the end for the armed opposition.

Syrian government forces, backed by Hezbollah, capture the strategic town of Qusair and launch an offensive in Homs province, seizing the village of Dabaa as they turn toward rebel-held areas in Homs and Aleppo.
Al-Qaeda leader Ayman al-Zawahiri urges jihadists fighting in Syria to unite and fight for the establishment of an anti-US Islamic state, saying the civil war has become a three-way conflict.

Austria announces it is withdrawing 377 U.N. peacekeepers from the Golan Heights after Syrian rebels briefly overran a crossing point near the border with Israel, deepening concerns the civil war is spreading to neighboring countries.
Syrian troops backed by Hezbollah fighters capture the central villages of Salhiyeh and Masoudiyeh north of Qusair, pressing their offensive in the opposition heartland.

Syrian National Coalition acting head George Sabra warns that Hezbollah's intervention in Syria is turning the war into a sectarian conflict between Sunnis and Shiites and says peace negotiations are not possible while Hezbollah and Iran fight alongside Assad's regime.

The leader of Syria's main opposition group warns that rebel fighters have been weakened and demoralized by recent tactical setbacks, and that aid from Iran, Russia, and Hezbollah is tipping the balance in the Syrian war toward President Bashar al-Assad's forces.
The UN launches the largest emergency appeal in its history, seeking $5bn to fund humanitarian aid for Syria as it warns that half the population will need assistance by the end of the year.

The Obama administration is considering resettling Syrian refugees as part of an international effort, though no formal request from the UN refugee agency has yet been received and no decision has been made.
Hezbollah's intervention in the Syrian civil war, including its role in the battle for Qusayr, is fueling Sunni-Shia violence in Lebanon and destabilizing the region.

Al-Qaida leader Ayman al-Zawahri orders the terror network's Syrian and Iraqi branches to remain separate, abolishing the attempted merger into the Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant, as Syrian rebels battle to capture a government air base in the north and the regime prepares an offensive to retake Aleppo.

Iraqi and Syrian territory is increasingly becoming a single battlefield, with cross-border attacks, fighters shuttling between the two countries, and growing sectarian violence, as nearly 2,000 lives have been lost across Iraq since the start of April.

Syrian government forces attack rebel positions in and around Aleppo province, including Minnigh Airport, as part of a widened offensive, while twin suicide bombings in Damascus kill 14 people and injure 31.
Lebanon is sheltering more than 1.2 million Syrians, a presence the caretaker social affairs minister calls the country's most dangerous challenge.
A column warns that Syria has become the center of a regional Sunni-Shiite sectarian conflict, with Hezbollah's intervention in Qusair prompting Sunni theologians to call for jihad in Syria.

As Syria's humanitarian crisis grows, international aid groups including Oxfam and Mercy Corps report collecting only a fraction of their fundraising goals, reflecting Americans' reluctance to engage with the conflict.

The White House says U.S. intelligence concluded with high confidence that the Assad regime used chemical weapons, including sarin, against rebel fighters in Syria multiple times in the past year, crossing what President Obama had called a "red line."
Russia says it is not convinced by U.S. claims that Syria used chemical weapons and calls the U.S. decision to send arms to some Syrian rebel groups unhelpful.

The United Nations reports 93,000 fatalities in Syria since the civil war began, as the Obama administration edges toward intervention amid evidence of chemical weapons use and recent pro-Assad gains including the fall of Qusayr.
Syrian government troops launch their heaviest assault in months on Aleppo, attacking the rebel-held Sakhour district with tanks and heavy artillery.
The Obama administration decides to supply small arms to antigovernment forces in Syria after concluding that President Bashar al-Assad's troops used chemical weapons against them.
Syria and Russia reject US allegations that Syrian government forces used chemical weapons, calling the claims fabricated and warning they will escalate the conflict.
Syrian government forces captured the rebel-held suburb of Ahmadiyeh near the Damascus international airport as part of an offensive to secure the capital.
Syrian rebels besiege predominantly Kurdish towns and villages around Afrin in northwest Syria, causing shortages of food and medicine and raising fears of an ethnic war between Kurds and Arabs.

Syrian Kurdish minority has carved out de facto autonomy in their areas, creating their own police forces and license plates, while increasingly clashing with Sunni rebels who have besieged a pocket of Kurdish towns and villages in northwest Syria.
As of June 2013, more than 90,000 Syrians had been killed according to the United Nations amid the Syrian uprising that began in March 2011.

Syria’s Kurdish minority has carved out de facto autonomy in Kurdish areas amid the civil war, creating police forces and license plates and openly promoting Kurdish language and culture, while clashes with Sunni rebels threaten to expand into an ethnic war.

Syrian rebels attack a main highway in northern Syria to try to cut off a major supply line for President Bashar Assad's forces, as Assad's troops backed by Hezbollah begin an offensive to regain the rebel-dominated north.

Russian President Vladimir Putin tours a new production facility for components of S-300 and S-400 surface-to-air missile systems, including the modernized S-300 that Syria has ordered and Russia is withholding under international pressure.

The U.K. used the G-8 summit to galvanize $1.5 billion in humanitarian aid for Syrian refugees, including $275 million from Britain, as the U.N. launched its largest ever humanitarian appeal of $1.7 billion.
Lebanese President Michel Suleiman calls on Hezbollah to withdraw its fighters from Syria, warning that further involvement in the civil war would fuel instability in Lebanon.

A bipartisan group of U.S. senators introduces legislation to block the Defense Department and intelligence agencies from funding operations in Syria, opposing the Obama administration's plan to arm rebels.
The European Commission warns the world is "sleepwalking" into the greatest ever refugee crisis as at least 1.66 million Syrians have fled the bloodshed to neighbouring countries.
Syrian government forces step up their offensive against rebel strongholds north of Damascus while opposition fighters declare their own offensive in Aleppo.
Car bombs and suicide bombers strike a military airbase in Aleppo and pro-government areas of Damascus, killing at least 25 people amid escalating battles for control of Syria's two largest cities.

A rift between Syria's Nusra Front and al Qaeda's Iraqi wing, the Islamic State of Iraq, over a merger and leadership dispute may lead to open conflict among jihadis fighting President Bashar al-Assad.
Syrian forces loyal to President Bashar al-Assad carry out mortar, artillery, and air strikes on rebel-held eastern districts of Damascus, focusing on Zamalka and Irbin.

UN envoy Lakhdar Brahimi mediates Russia-US talks in Geneva on the Syrian conflict, hoping to relaunch a peace conference after July, though he could not be certain basic questions about how and when to hold it could be immediately resolved.
Saudi Arabia's foreign minister says the kingdom cannot be silent about Iranian intervention in Syria and calls for rebels to be offered military aid.
A UN team sent to Turkey reports 10 separate incidents of chemical weapon use by the Syrian government, according to UN diplomats.

Syria's Kurds are carving out a self-governed zone in northeastern Syria, creating security forces, municipalities, courts, and Kurdish-language classes, and controlling oil fields and border-crossing revenue, as the decay of President Bashar al-Assad's government creates an opportunity for them.

A bipartisan group of U.S. lawmakers pushes a resolution to stall the Obama administration's move to arm certain factions of the Syrian opposition, as the CIA is reported to be moving weapons to Jordan in anticipation of arming small groups of Syrian rebels in about a month.
UN-appointed inspectors, blocked from entering Syria, are in Turkey to gather information about possible chemical weapons use in the Syrian civil war.

Syrian government troops launch a major artillery barrage on the city of Homs, hitting buildings near a 13th-century mosque as they press an assault on rebel-held areas, with activists saying Lebanese Hezbollah guerrillas had joined the fighting.
Hopes for an international peace conference on Syria fade as the date keeps slipping and diplomats say it is unclear whether the conference will take place at all.
Syrian regime forces launch a military offensive on the rebel-held Khalidiyah district of Homs, with state television reporting "great progress" amid heavy shelling and airstrikes.
Syrian government forces backed by jets launch a major offensive on rebel-held areas of Homs, a center of the uprising, in a drive to secure an axis connecting Damascus to the Mediterranean.
Assad's forces pound Sunni Muslim rebels in Homs with artillery and airstrikes on the second day of their offensive in central Syria, as rebels largely repelled a ground attack the previous day.

U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry says the U.S. and Russia have agreed to hold a peace conference on Syria after August to seek a peaceful settlement to the civil war, though details remain to be worked out.

Syrian government troops backed by Hezbollah militants launch a major artillery barrage on rebel-held areas of Homs, trapping thousands of civilians and prompting warnings of a humanitarian catastrophe.
Israel carried out an airstrike near Latakia, Syria, targeting Russian-made Yakhont anti-ship missiles that U.S. officials said were sold to Syria.
UN agencies warn that four million Syrians will need urgent food aid as the civil war devastates crop and livestock production.
Russian President Vladimir Putin says Egypt is moving towards civil war, comparing it to Syria which he says is already in the grips of civil war.
Syrian government forces and rebels fight intensified battles in the strategic city of Homs, as the army offensive aims to link Damascus with Assad's coastal strongholds.

Syrian government troops pounded rebel-held areas in Homs for the tenth consecutive day, with a suicide car bomb striking a predominantly Alawite and Christian neighborhood, as the government rejected a proposed Ramadan cease-fire.

Russia's UN envoy says Russian scientific analysis indicates a projectile that hit Khan al-Assal near Aleppo on March 19 contained sarin and was most likely fired by rebels, while the US casts doubt on the findings and calls for full UN access to suspected chemical weapons sites in Syria.

A report by senior British lawmakers warns that Syria's vast chemical weapons stockpiles could fall into the hands of militants with links to terrorism if President Bashar Assad is toppled, with potentially catastrophic consequences.
The opposition Syrian National Coalition denies Russian allegations that rebel fighters fired a sarin-laden projectile at Khan al-Assal in Aleppo in March, calling for U.N. inspectors to investigate.
The United Nations accepts the Syrian government's invitation for talks by two senior U.N. officials on the purported use of chemical weapons in Syria's civil war.
Al-Qaeda kills a rival commander as infighting among Syrian rebels grows.
Syrian government forces bombed the rebel-held town of Saraqeb in northern Idlib province for a third straight day, killing at least five people including three children, according to activists.

Western-backed opposition fighters and al-Qaida-linked rebels battle each other in Aleppo for control of a key checkpoint, in the latest eruption of infighting among forces trying to topple President Bashar Assad's regime.
Infighting between al-Qaida-linked groups and mainstream Syrian rebels, including the killings of two rebel commanders, is undermining the revolt against President Bashar Assad.

The United Nations reports that the Syrian civil war has caused the worst refugee crisis since the Rwandan genocide, with an average of 6,000 people per day fleeing the country and at least 6.8 million Syrians in need of urgent aid.
Rebel infighting in Syria, including clashes and assassinations between Al-Qaeda-linked fighters and mainstream Free Syrian Army rebels, undermines the revolt against President Bashar Assad.

United Nations officials state that war crimes and crimes against humanity are "the rule" in Syria, as the civil war creates the world's worst refugee crisis in 20 years with 6,000 people fleeing daily and 93,000 total killed.
U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry visits the Zaatari refugee camp in Jordan, where Syrian refugees plead with him for help.
The head of a U.N. chemical weapons investigation team, Ake Sellstrom, is set to travel to Damascus next week to discuss his probe into allegations of chemical arms use in Syria's civil war.

A Syrian Kurdish group says it aims to set up an independent council to run Kurdish regions until Syria's civil war has ended, with a final decision expected in a week or two and elections planned within three to four months if an agreement is reached.

U.S. and European officials warn that growing numbers of radicalized foreign fighters traveling to Syria to join opposition groups such as al-Nusra Front raise concerns they may return home to carry out terrorist attacks.
A rebel group in Syria with links to Al Qaeda reportedly released hundreds of kidnapped Kurdish civilians after clashes with Kurdish militiamen in the northern Syrian town of Tal Abyad.
The United States weighs arming Syrian rebels.
